correctness.rationale: The bipartite Hall description reduces the polytope to one Hall facet and the coordinate cube in its true (2n-1)-dimensional Euclidean affine space. Intrinsic projected normal lengths ell=sqrt((2n-1)/(2n)) and h=sqrt(n/2) give unconditional box and Hall radius obstructions. Explicit centers attain their minimum; saturation proves their uniqueness. The threshold equation has no integer solution by divisibility. Genuine active facets are verified with Mori Proposition 3.4; 15 integer parameter cases passed independently solved LPs and small-dimensional brute matching/facet-rank tests.

value.rationale: A canonical Hall obstruction of a natural graph-polytope family has its exact intrinsic Euclidean inball classified for all integer pairs. The theorem identifies an explicit critical deleted-block size, a genuine rigid switch from all 4n coordinate-facet contacts to 2n coordinate plus Hall contacts, and unique extremal centers. These metric facts are not determined by the established facet list or f-vectors alone, making the classification a motivated structural geometric result.
